application_type: Householder planning application (Town and Country Planning Act 1990)
proposal_description: Erection of a two-storey front extension with rooms in the roof and a basement beneath, forming a new principal frontage to Ashley Close; first-floor and roof extension to the existing side wing; rear dormer; alterations to fenestration, forecourt, boundary wall and gate; removal of the porch, chimney and front boundary piers. The side-wing front wall and roof edge are set back 900 mm in the saved model, subject to survey reconciliation. Matching red-brown facing brick and dark brown-grey roof tiles, with tile-hung dormer cheeks and front panels. Existing garden buildings retained. Pool, spa and loggia excluded from this application.
north_basis: Least-squares registration of the model to the north-up OS extract (proposal/street-registration/registration.json): model +x bears 82.65°, so model +y bears 352.9°. Confirm against the purchased OS extract.
red_line_source: navigation.site.outline_m (HM Land Registry title plan K568939 traced and registered)
rear_strip_basis: The rear garden strip is drawn inside the same red line as on the title plan; the coloured strips at its north-west corner on the title plan are rights of way, not separate titles — verify against the register.

designations.basis: Green Belt: owner confirms the site is outside. Read-only Sevenoaks public GIS screening on 25 September 2026, using the existing approximate model-to-BNG registration, shows no plot overlap with The Vine conservation area or nearby Article 4 areas. These are map checks, not formal land-charge verification. TPO 19/1987 (T4 cherry and G1 group) is mapped beside the east/rear boundary; legal coverage, surviving tree identity and root protection require survey and council/arboricultural confirmation. Historic England NHLE screening finds no listed-building point/polygon on the reconstructed plot; this does not determine curtilage, setting or local listing. Current Environment Agency flood-zone data returns no Zone 2/3 polygon within the plot plus 100 m, supporting river/sea Flood Zone 1 map screening. Natural England boundary screening places the plot outside Kent Downs National Landscape, about 675 m away; setting effects are not assessed. Environment Agency surface-water spatial-planning WMS screening shows no mapped extent across the approximate plot in the present-day or 2070s upper-end climate scenarios; these are area-level datasets, not an individual-property flood assessment. Groundwater, sewer flooding, drainage changes and basement suitability remain unverified. See proposal/redesigns/research/RESEARCH.md. Further official GIS screening on 3 October 2026 places the approximate plot inside the urban confines and outside the Green Belt, local-list polygons and Article 4 polygons. The nearest locally listed asset identified is 3 Vine Avenue (10172), approximately 42.5 m from the modelled plot; its setting requires assessment. This is map screening, not a land-charge or measured-boundary certificate.

original_dwelling.basis: Existing reconstructed house is the comparison baseline, not a verified original-house baseline. Historic application leads 83/01218/HIST, 83/01336/HIST and 84/00546/HIST require notices and approved drawings; construction date and extension history are unverified.

To be confirmed by measured survey before submission.
levels_basis: Site terrain and ground levels are model estimates, not a measured topographical survey; verify all levels, thresholds and boundaries.

visibility_splays.basis: The shown 2.4 m x 25 m splay is an unverified concept, not an accepted 30 mph design. Manual for Streets Table 7.1 gives 25 m at 20 mph and 43 m at 30 mph. Confirm observed speeds, highway geometry and the required splays with KCC Highways.

trees.basis: Tree locations and canopies are illustrative model objects, not a BS5837 survey. Labels are model references, not survey or TPO IDs; heights and RPAs are deliberately not certified. Match a consistent survey inventory across existing/proposed plans before submission.

materials.roof: Weathered dark brown-grey roof tiles with subtle tile-to-tile variation to match the existing house in material, colour, profile, size and coursing, consistent with neighbouring houses; existing roof covering retained where shown
materials.dormers: Tile-hung cheeks and front panels to match the existing weathered dark brown-grey roof tiles; dark flat roof membrane and metal flashings; black window frames
materials.windows_doors: Bronze-black powder-coated aluminium frames, clear double glazing; pale oak external doors
materials.hard_landscape: Resin-bound gravel forecourt, limestone paving, permeable court paving
materials.boundary: Matching red-brown brick front wall, 1.95 m (26 courses), with oak-slatted sliding gate; existing fences and hedges retained
materials.privacy: Side-wing west bedroom windows and new-wing east windows facing neighbours obscure-glazed below 1.7 m; opening restrictions and sightlines to be verified.

front_wing_case.summary: The proposal retains the modelled 8.05 m ridge and 5.35 m eaves while adding a front wing and roof accommodation. The design intention is a new principal frontage at the cul-de-sac head, with an open courtyard and a legible retained house. These features support an argument to test, not a finding of acceptability. The modelled projection is approximately 16 m beyond the original front, with approximately 5.3 m remaining to the front boundary wall. Surveyed street and oblique views must establish prominence and building-line relationships.
front_wing_case.basis: Owner instruction, 3 October 2026: hold the current planning-model house envelope fixed and strengthen its case first. Assess any unresolved harm explicitly; reduction is a later fallback, not authorised by this review.

precedents.description: Extensive remodelling, extensions, roof accommodation and basement works were accepted while retaining the house.
precedents.relevance: Conservation-area site with a generous plot. Officer report records approximately 10 m front setback, compared with approximately 5.3 m to the front boundary wall in Ashley's model. Approved dormers were described as modest.

precedents.description: An extension without a lowered ridge was accepted because the integrated roof form and surrounding context were suitable.
precedents.relevance: Screening, the open western plot and separation from neighbours mattered. The decision does not establish that matching ridge height alone makes a large front wing acceptable.

precedents.description: A deep front garage projection dominated the house and disrupted the street relationship despite a matching roof pitch. Screening did not overcome the harm.
precedents.relevance: The regular White Hart Wood frontage differs from Ashley's cul-de-sac head. Demonstrate that distinction with measured context rather than simply asserting it.

precedents.description: Street character was acceptable, but the extension would harm outlook from a neighbour's sole bedroom windows. Acceptable daylight and privacy did not cure oppressive outlook.
precedents.relevance: Different house form and window arrangement. The transferable lesson is to assess outlook separately, especially from single-aspect habitable rooms.

precedents.description: A significantly larger and taller replacement was accepted because its siting, lower hipped eaves, gaps and angled relationship avoided unacceptable effects.
precedents.relevance: Large plots and a backland setting differ from Ashley's visible frontage. This is evidence of context-dependent acceptance, not an allowance for equivalent enlargement.

precedents.description: The inspector accepted massing and modern design but rejected privacy effects associated with windows and raised outdoor areas.
precedents.relevance: The subsequent 22/02482/FUL committee approval followed window changes while retaining the bulk and form. This supports testing targeted amenity measures before assuming wholesale reduction is necessary.

precedents.description: A replacement dwelling was accepted against a substantial certified permitted-development fallback and its particular design advantages.
precedents.relevance: Green Belt and protected landscape: not Ashley's designation context. It demonstrates a mechanism for comparison, not a general demolition bonus or an applicable percentage allowance.

precedents.description: The replacement had less floorspace, footprint and slightly less volume than its fallback but greater upper-level massing and visual harm. A credible fallback did not compel approval.
precedents.relevance: Green Belt case. Do not import its Green Belt enlargement tests into Ashley's urban site; use only to explain why aggregate area or volume cannot replace visual assessment.

precedents.decision: Officer recommendation to grant, 3 May 2018; formal notice not verified
precedents.description: The officer accepted substantial additional width on balance, considering roof design, gaps and the particular relationships with neighbouring houses.
precedents.relevance: The upper front projection was about 1 m, compared with about 16 m beyond Ashley's original frontage. Proposed drawings are not proof of the present as-built arrangement.
